guidance: Use it to place a civil date on the Hijri calendar or to read a Hijri date in the Gregorian calendar. This is the arithmetic tabular calendar, so do not use it to fix the start of Ramadan, Eid or any other religious observance: those follow a sighted or officially announced month and can fall a day or two away, which is why the Umm al-Qura calendar exists. The page supports Gregorian 1600 to 2200 only, the window over which its epoch arithmetic was checked, and it takes no time of day or location, so a Hijri day is treated as beginning at midnight for conversion purposes.
method: The tabular (arithmetic) Islamic calendar counts days from a fixed epoch: 1 Muharram 1 AH is 19 July 622 in the proleptic Gregorian calendar, a Friday, which is fixed day 227015. Years follow a 30-year cycle of 10,631 days with eleven leap years in cycle positions 2, 5, 7, 10, 13, 16, 18, 21, 24, 26 and 29, so a year is leap when (11 x year + 14) mod 30 is less than 11 and is then 355 days long instead of 354. Odd-numbered months have 30 days and even-numbered months 29, except that Dhu al-Hijjah, the twelfth month, has 30 days in a leap year; the day of the year on which a month begins is therefore ceil(29.5 x (month - 1)), which gives 0, 30, 59, 89, 118, 148, 177, 207, 236, 266, 295 and 325. A Hijri date converts to a fixed day as epoch - 1 + (year - 1) x 354 + floor((3 + 11 x year) / 30) + that month offset + day, and the inverse starts from year = floor((30 x (fixed - epoch) + 10646) / 10631), steps to the year whose 1 Muharram is at or before the day, and walks the month lengths. The weekday is the fixed day modulo 7 with Sunday as zero, so the two directions share one continuous day count and cannot drift apart. The epoch reproduces 1 Muharram 1 AH as Friday 19 July 622, and the arithmetic is the four-arithmetic variant used by the Kuwaiti algorithm and by Fourmilab's converter. Because the calendar is arithmetic rather than observational, an official Umm al-Qura date can differ by a day or two; the result also treats a Hijri day as starting at midnight instead of sunset. Gregorian years 1600 to 2200 are supported, Hijri years 1008 to 1627, and a Hijri date whose civil day falls outside that window is refused. Everything is calculated in the browser; nothing is uploaded or stored.
